keys.q: Two independent bases; A is already diagonally biased and B owns a taller opposite stance.
keys.a: A pelvis sits left/back of lead hand; B pelvis sits right/back of near hand. Negative space is intentionally wide.

keys.q: A spends COM and stance depth before contact; B braces without mirroring.
keys.a: A lead hand arcs forward/up while rear hand and pelvis countercoil down/back. B compresses only enough to receive force.

keys.q: Contact acquisition is an authored event before custody transfer; both still own ground.
keys.a: The seam appears inside the reachable envelope, not at farthest extension; force points through B's near shoulder toward pelvis.

keys.q: Second body is now inside A's locked frame; A rear foot becomes explicit world anchor before the pivot.
keys.a: A front side rises while rear root stays fixed; B pelvis is already pulled off its neutral vertical stack.

keys.q: A sinks under the relationship frame; B loses far support before any release is permitted.
keys.a: Force axis steepens down/right while A rear root remains invariant; B far foot is visually late and no longer authoritative.

keys.q: The locked relationship rotates around A's pinned rear root while B support peels into a trailing toe drag.
keys.a: A front foot steps around the pin; B becomes diagonal/horizontal and trails behind the seam instead of mirroring A.

keys.q: B is fully unrooted, but custody remains locked. This is the visible proof that pivot and release are separate events.
keys.a: Shared force axis has rotated above horizontal; B legs lag below/behind torso while A torso counterleans over the pinned root.

keys.q: A holds the late release threshold for readability; B remains suspended and cannot self-author the root.
keys.a: The frame rotates past apex while contact seam survives. A's shoulders lag pelvis rotation; B distal limbs drag behind the shared arc.

keys.q: Release is a later authored causal fork: B travels outward while A recoils opposite the outgoing line.
keys.a: A torso folds left/down and keeps one plant; B opens right/up with trailing feet. Recoil is not reverse pivot interpolation.

keys.q: A continues a smaller recoil overshoot while B distal limbs lag the torso's outgoing arc.
keys.a: Spacing grows nonlinearly after release; A's free hand overshoots backward while B rear-side hand/foot trail.

keys.q: B catches on one foot while upper body and far foot continue past it; A has not yet recovered its stack.
keys.a: B pelvis drops behind the first catch and torso leans outward; A still carries recoil debt in shoulder/hand placement.

keys.q: B second foot arrives after torso overshoot; A starts restacking but free hand remains late.
keys.a: B torso counter-rotates over newly widened base; A shoulder and hand lag root recovery by one authored phase.

keys.q: Both regain partial independent support at new addresses, but neither returns to neutral: A remains pitched into the throw-side debt while B settles late over a mismatched base.
keys.a: A keeps shoulder ahead of pelvis with rear support still dominant; B keeps head/torso behind the first-catch line and rear limb trailing. The loop ends with visible debt, not an idle reset.
